Round half away from zero

Source: R/precision.R
round_half_up.Rd

round_half_up() rounds x to digits decimal places, rounding a value that lies exactly half-way (e.g. 6.25 to one decimal place) away from zero, which is how SAS rounds and what most readers of a clinical table expect. Base round() (and sprintf()) round such ties to the even digit instead (6.25 becomes 6.2), and values that are ties in decimal but not in binary (e.g. 6.35, stored as 6.3499999...) are rounded down.

Usage

round_half_up(x, digits = 0L)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector. NA values are returned as NA.

digits

A single non-negative number of decimal places. Defaults to 0.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length as x.

Details

A small tolerance (1e-9, or a few machine epsilons for very large values) absorbs binary representation error, so any value that is a tie in decimal is treated as a tie. For percentages of whole counts this is exact for any realistic denominator.

Examples

round_half_up(c(6.25, 6.35, 0.5, 2.5, -2.5), 1)
#> [1]  6.3  6.4  0.5  2.5 -2.5
round_half_up(c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, -2.5))
#> [1]  1  2  3 -3
# Base R rounds ties to even
round(c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, -2.5))
#> [1]  0  2  2 -2
